title: Multiple-root fan-out conditions
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $G$ and $E$ be finite gate lists, and let $R$ be a list of natural-number roots. Every old vertex $v$ with $n\le v<n+|G|$ has fan-out zero in $E$, and every vertex $v\ge n$ has fan-out at most one in $E$. Each root $r$ in $R$ with $r\ge n$ has fan-out zero, and every root is either below $n$ or at least $n+|G|$. Every vertex $v$ with $n+|G|\le v<n+|G|+|E|$ that is not in $R$ has fan-out exactly one in $E$.
hypotheses_covered: old gate list G and extension gate list E
old vertices in [n,n+|G|) have fan-out zero in E
every vertex at least n has fan-out at most one in E
each listed root at least n has fan-out zero
each listed root is below n or at least n+|G|
new vertices in [n+|G|, n+|G|+|E|) not listed as roots have fan-out one
